main_text.l: 1 Hæc admonitio non solùm pertinet ad
reges, principes, gubernatores ciuitatum, &
episcopos ecclesiarum, sed etiam ad patres
& matres familiâs. Omnes enim illi man-
fueti & prudentes esse debent, non crudeles
in subditos, vel inexorabiles, aut saftuosi, o-
mnia perturbantes ex ira vel impatientia; do-
mesticos præcipuè, quos præstat piè tracta-
re, & ædificare, non opprimere vel vastare.
Crudele & superbum animal leo est, atque
tyrannicum, qualem non decet Præla tum
esse, sed manfuetum & modestum, ad bene-
faciendum propensiorem, quàm ad nocen-
dum, ducere potius volentem in suam sen-
tentiam, quàm trahere violenter. Sufcipite
infirmos, Paulus dicit Thessalonicensibus,
patientes estote ad omnes. Iesaias quoque:

page.notes: The woodcut initial is read as N; the first letter is uncertain. The reading "infane" is printed as such. The word "domesticos" is split across lines ("do" / "mesticos") without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The line "Præla tum" is split without a hyphen and is written whole ("Prælatum"). Long s is rendered as s throughout. The catchword "Væ" is at the lower right. The printed "sæuitas" is written sævitas, and "Ecclef." is written Eccles.
